intent: Maintain the current geometry with 7 sensors and increased sensor size and wheel track, as these provide good line detection resolution and turning stability. The previous race data and integrator feedback indicate the main issues are controller tuning rather than geometry. Therefore, no geometry changes are made this iteration to isolate controller improvements. The goal is to confirm that the geometry supports improved controller tuning without introducing new variables.
rationale: The previous iteration increased sensor count to 7, sensor size to 0.016, and wheel track to 0.15, which improved line detection resolution and turning stability. However, the robot still went off track due to controller issues, not geometry faults. The integrator feedback recommends tuning controller gains and reducing base speed for better steering precision and stability. Since the geometry changes are appropriate and beneficial, I keep the geometry unchanged to allow the integrator to focus on controller tuning. This approach isolates the effect of controller changes and avoids confounding factors. I expect the geometry to continue supporting good line detection and turning stability, enabling the controller to improve performance. I request measurements of completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, and line_loss_events to evaluate the combined effect of geometry and controller tuning in the next race.
